title: The Omnivore's Dilemma: A Natural History of Four Meals
reason: This book directly aligns with my specialty in agronomy and cross-disciplinary approach to food systems and agriculture. As someone working in media and journalism with focus on agronomy, understanding the industrial food production systems, supply chains, and sustainability issues covered in Pollan's work is essential for investigative reporting and informed analysis. The book's exploration of food security and agricultural practices is particularly relevant to my context in Sub-Saharan Africa where food systems and agricultural development are critical socioeconomic issues. Given my value-driven spending posture and focus on security as a personal value, this intellectually rigorous examination of what we eat and where it comes from represents high-value knowledge investment for both professional development and personal understanding.
